facts.statement: Karatausuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the atoposaurid crocodylomorphs.
facts.quote: Karatausuchus is an extinct genus of atoposaurid crocodylomorph.

facts.statement: The animal is known from a single fossil specimen found in the Karabastau Svita near Mikhailovka in the Karatau Mountains of southern Kazakhstan.
facts.quote: It is known from a single specimen discovered in the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian - Kimmeridgian) Karabastau Svita from the vicinity of Mikhailovka in the Karatau Mountains of southern Kazakhstan.

facts.statement: The type specimen, cataloged as PIN 25858/1, is a complete but poorly preserved juvenile skeleton that may retain some soft tissue.
facts.quote: The type specimen is PIN 25858/1, a complete but poorly preserved juvenile skeleton with some possible soft tissue preservation.

facts.statement: The skeleton is notable for possessing over 90 teeth, while other anatomical features are hard to identify.
facts.quote: It is notable for having over 90 teeth, but its other anatomical details are difficult to discern.

facts.statement: This individual specimen was estimated to be 160 mm in length.
facts.quote: The length of this individual is estimated at 160 mm.

facts.statement: The genus was described in 1976 by Mikhail Efimov, with the type species named K. sharovi.
facts.quote: Karatausuchus was described in 1976 by Mikhail Efimov, and the type species is K. sharovi.

facts.statement: Karatausuchus lived during the Oxfordian stage, between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Karatausuchus is classified within the parent group Crocodyliformes.
